title: A Bridge for the Compass
premise: In 1898, on a fog-bound trading post between two empires, Mirabel Montrose dives for pearls by day and hides her literacy by night, knowing an educated indentured girl draws dangerous attention. When a wounded courier arrives bearing letters in the handwriting of Captain Elias Thorne — the man who freed her father's debt years ago and was since reported drowned at war — she learns he is alive, branded a traitor, and hiding within reach. Bound by a promise made in peacetime, Mirabel must choose between the company that owns her contract and the truth that could free them both, smuggling Thorne across the strait as the company's agents close in. In the end she burns her own indenture papers to light their escape across the bridge at low tide, choosing love and identity over the loyalty she was bought into.
about_author: Felix Voss is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading ledgers before turning to fiction. Voss writes historical fiction about people history forgot to name, drawing on salvaged letters and port records from the late nineteenth century.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet her diving the cold shallows for the Meridian Trading Company, concealing that she can read, and tending the memory of Captain Thorne, who once paid her father's debt. A storm wrecks a boat on the rocks; among the survivors is a half-drowned stranger clutching an oilskin packet. Emotional beat: quiet endurance cracked open by fate's intrusion.

chapters.title: Handwriting of a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The stranger, delirious with fever, begs her to deliver letters to 'the lighthouse keeper' — letters in Thorne's unmistakable hand, dated after his reported death. Reading them in secret, Mirabel learns Thorne lives, declared enemy for refusing a massacre order. The company's factor begins asking questions about the wreck. Emotional beat: dread blooming into resolve; the promise reawakens.

chapters.title: What the Tide Owes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mirabel and Thorne, hidden at the lighthouse. They meet at last; he asks not for rescue but for her silence, unwilling to endanger her. The factor discovers the missing packet and accuses Mirabel of theft, threatening her contract and her father's freedom. She lies to his face for the first time. Emotional beat: love against duty sharpening into open defiance.

chapters.title: A Bridge for the Compass
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax and resolution. With the factor's men searching the post, Mirabel steals back her own indenture papers and burns them to signal Thorne from the tower. At low tide they cross the old causeway as lanterns sweep the water behind them. He offers her passage; she chooses it freely, no longer owned. Emotional beat: liberation — loyalty to truth outlasting loyalty to masters.
